Name: Anna Cummins
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I learned that students are more willing to write than what we think, especially when it's about themselves. I often get stuck on the formal writing and then kids struggle and lose self-confidence when it comes to writing. I need to be incorporating more freedom in writing throughout the year to keep the self-esteem up!

Share one artifact or anecdote from trying out your chosen strategy (e.g., a piece of student work, notes from your Writer’s Notebook, a classroom snapshot, or a brief story from the experience).:
What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

How can I incorporate this type of writing to meet standards and not just be a "for fun" writing thing? Do older students respond the same as younger students when it comes to this strategy? I definitely want to try out the argumentative area for Module 1. I'm wondering if the response to the writing will be the same.
